title: Post-incident follow-up: Canary routing misconfiguration and rollback failure during model rollout
creator: Avery Chen
description: This ticket captures the postmortem analysis and actionable follow-ups for the model rollout incident on 2026-02-19 where an intended canary deployment incorrectly routed majority traffic to the experimental model variant and subsequent rollback attempts failed. The document includes timeline, root causes, mitigations already applied, and a prioritized action item list with owners and deadlines.
incident_summary: During a routine canary rollout of model v2026-02-B to the hosted fleet in us-west-2, the rollout configuration omitted the explicit canary weight field. A router-side bug treated the absent field as 'full-traffic' for compatible variants, sending ~95% of production traffic to the canary variant. Within 7 minutes we observed a 12% median latency regression and an increase in 5xx errors from 0.2% to 3.1%. Automated canary monitors tripped alerts and a manual rollback was initiated, but the rollback process encountered a version-pinning race: the new rollback job attempted to pin the previous stable model while autoscaler concurrently removed nodes, causing a transient state where neither model was warm and requests failed. Overall customer-facing errors lasted ~28 minutes. No data leakage or exfiltration detected.

root_cause: Combination of (1) a templating bug in the deployment manifest generator that resulted in an omitted 'traffic_weight' field for canary rollouts, (2) a router behavior bug that treated absent canary weight as '100%' allocation rather than '0%' or 'invalid', and (3) a race condition in the model pin/rollback control path when autoscaler and rollback job executed concurrently, causing both model variants to be unready.
immediate_mitigations_applied: Reverted routing rules to pin stable model via force-deploy to warmed capacity (manual override)
Disabled templated canary deployment in CI until schema validation was added
Rolled out a temporary router guard that rejects rollouts without an explicit 'traffic_weight' field
corrective_actions: Patch router to default to safe behavior on absent weight (reject deployment and require explicit weight)
Add strict JSON schema validation to canary deployment manifests in CI; block merge on failures
Fix race in model pinning logic: implement optimistic locking in model registry and add retries with backoff
Enhance rollback runbook with a 'force-warm' path that pre-warms stable model replicas before switching traffic
Create alerting for mismatch between declared rollout weight and observed traffic distributions
Add end-to-end integration test simulating autoscaler + rollback concurrency

testing_and_validation_plan: Unit and integration tests will be added for the router to assert safe default behavior. CI will include schema validation for canary manifests and a new stage that spins up a lightweight simulated canary traffic generator to verify that traffic weights are honored. The model registry changes will include a chaos-style test to validate pin/unpin under concurrent autoscaler operations.
risk_and_followups: Risk: delayed completion of optimistic locking allows another similar incident if autoscaler behavior changes. Follow-up: schedule a cross-team review with infra/autoscaler owners (ENG-4680) to validate prewarming timeouts and autoscaler policies. Also consider adding canary rollout 'dry-run' feature in Console to preview routing decisions before activating.
